title: 4. Article 2 – Admission or Establishment of New States

blocks.content: Parliament may by law admit into the Union, or establish, new States on such terms and conditions as it thinks fit.

rows: Territories outside the Union of India
Existing territories within the Union of India
Admission or establishment of new states
Internal reorganisation, alteration of boundaries, area, or names
Admission of Sikkim into the Union of India
Bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh to form Telangana

items: Crucial Distinction: Article 2 deals with the admission or establishment of new states that were NOT previously part of India, whereas Article 3 deals with internal reorganization of existing states.

35th and 36th Constitutional Amendment Acts (1974 & 1975): Sikkim was introduced as an 'associate state' via the 35th Amendment and fully admitted into the Union of India as a full state via the 36th Amendment.
Laws made under Article 2 are passed by Parliament with a simple majority and are not considered constitutional amendments under Article 368.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 2 empowers Parliament to admit into the Union, or establish, new States on such terms and conditions as it thinks fit.
It confers two distinct powers: the power to admit existing states into the Union and the power to establish entirely new states.
Article 2 relates specifically to the admission or establishment of territories that are not already part of the Union of India.
This provision gives Parliament wide discretion in determining the terms and conditions for admitting foreign or non-Union territories.
